title: Model bundle manifest 1
description: The `manifest.json` at the root of an ImageProcessor model bundle. A bundle is an immutable, content-addressed tarball whose digest is the SHA-256 of the tarball itself; `manifest.sig` is the Ed25519 detached signature over the exact bytes of this document. The manifest is the only thing a bundle may say about itself, and it is verified, never trusted: the component checks the tarball digest, then the signature when the profile requires one, then extracts under path, count, size, and ratio limits, then checks every per-file digest against `files`, then this schema, and only then decides whether the declared task family and providers are supported. No bundle-supplied code is ever executed.

schemaVersion.description: The manifest contract version. The component refuses a bundle whose version it does not implement rather than guessing at the shape.

modelId.description: The model's published id. A route's `modelRef.id` matches it.

version.description: The model's published version. Identity on the wire is the tarball digest, so a version is a label for people, not the thing the component pins to.

files.title: Per-file digests
files.description: Every file the bundle carries, keyed by its path relative to the bundle root, with its SHA-256 as the value. Extraction checks each one; a file that is present but unlisted, or listed but absent, fails staging.

minOnnxRuntime.description: The lowest ONNX Runtime version that can load this model. A device running an older runtime refuses the bundle instead of failing on the first inference.

providersPermitted.description: The execution providers this model may run on, in preference order. Staging refuses the bundle when none of them appears in the device's `runtime.providers`.

providerPolicy.description: How strictly `providersPermitted` binds. `requireListed`: the session must be assigned one of the listed providers, and a route whose device cannot supply one is blocked rather than run elsewhere. `preferListed`: the listed providers are tried in order and `CPUExecutionProvider` may serve as a fallback, which the device honors only when `runtime.allowCpuOnly` is set.

inputs.description: The model's input tensors, as the graph declares them.

outputs.description: The model's output tensors, as the graph declares them. The task family interprets them, so an output set no family can read is refused at staging.

dynamicBatch.description: Whether the input shapes carry a dynamic batch axis. The scheduler micro-batches only when this is `true`, so a static-batch model is never handed more than one image at a time.

family.description: The built-in task family that turns the raw outputs into the normalized result the decision rules evaluate.

familyParams.description: The parameters the declared family needs. Its shape depends on `family`; see the per-family conditions at the end of this schema.

maxResultItems.description: How many items the normalized output may carry: classes, detections, or segment classes. It bounds both the published message and the evidence sidecar.

estimatedDeviceMiB.description: The publisher's estimate of the device memory one resident session needs. GPU admission starts from this number and refines it with measurements once the model has run.

measuredDeviceMiB.title: Measured memory profiles
measuredDeviceMiB.description: Measured profiles per GPU class, which supersede `estimatedDeviceMiB` on a matching device.

loadPeakMiB.description: The transient peak observed while the session loads.

steadyMiB.description: The steady-state footprint of the resident session.

warmup.description: The golden samples a session runs before it serves any job. A model that cannot reproduce its own goldens on the target provider degrades its routes instead of answering.

compatibilityKeys.title: Engine cache compatibility keys
compatibilityKeys.description: The dimensions a cached execution-provider engine is keyed by, as a flat map of names to values. A cached engine is reused only when every key matches the current device, driver, and runtime. Well-known keys are `precision`, `shapeProfile`, `gpuClass`, `cudaVersion`, `tensorrtVersion`, and `onnxruntimeVersion`.

keyId.description: The signing key that produced `manifest.sig`, named as it appears in the device's `signing.trustedKeys`. It is `null` on an unsigned bundle, which a device with `signing.required` refuses.

transformVersion.description: The version of the decode and preprocessing contract this bundle expects. It is recorded on every job and every result, so a preprocessing change shows up as a different transform version rather than as a silent shift in the numbers.

name.description: The tensor's name in the graph.

shape.description: The tensor's shape. A positive integer is a fixed axis; a string names a dynamic axis, and the name `N` is reserved for the batch axis the scheduler batches along.

preprocess.title: Decode and preprocessing
preprocess.description: How an executor cell turns decoded pixels into the model's input tensor. The component applies exactly this, so two bundles that share a transform version and a preprocess block produce comparable numbers.

inputName.description: The input tensor the preprocessed image binds to. Omit it on a single-input model.

mode.description: How the source image reaches the model's input size. `stretch`: scale both axes independently. `letterbox`: scale to fit, then pad with `padValue`, which preserves aspect ratio and is what box coordinates are un-letterboxed from. `centerCrop`: scale the short side, then crop the center. `none`: feed the image as decoded, which needs a fully dynamic input shape.

width.description: The model input width in pixels.

height.description: The model input height in pixels.

interpolation.description: The resampling filter. It is part of the numeric contract, so changing it changes the transform version.

padValue.description: The per-channel fill for `letterbox` padding, in the source pixel scale before normalization.

normalize.title: Normalize
normalize.description: The affine mapping applied per channel as `(pixel * scale - mean) / std`.

scale.description: The factor applied to each raw pixel value before mean subtraction. The default maps `0..255` onto `0..1`.

mean.description: The per-channel mean subtracted after scaling, in channel order.

std.description: The per-channel standard deviation divided out after mean subtraction, in channel order.

layout.description: The axis order of the input tensor.

colorOrder.description: The channel order the model expects. Decoded images are RGB, so `BGR` reverses them.

dtype.description: The element type of the input tensor after preprocessing.

channels.description: How many channels the model takes. `1` converts to grayscale.

decisionRules.title: Decision rules
decisionRules.description: JSONPath expressions evaluated over the normalized task output. A rule that cannot evaluate yields `HOLD`, never `CLEAR`, which is why `outcome.whenUnevaluable` has only one value.

pass.description: The expression that decides `decision.pass`. It is a JSONPath over the normalized output, optionally compared against a literal or against `threshold`.

confidence.description: The JSONPath whose value becomes `decision.confidence`. Omit it when the family produces no single confidence.

threshold.description: The number `pass` compares against, republished as `decision.threshold` so a consumer can see the bar that was applied.

whenPass.description: The outcome when `pass` evaluates true. An advisory model sets it to `HOLD` so a pass still requires a human.

whenFail.description: The outcome when `pass` evaluates false. `CLEAR` is not available here.

whenUnevaluable.description: The outcome when the rules cannot be evaluated at all. It is always `HOLD`.

input.description: The raw input tensor, as little-endian binary matching `dtype` and `shape`.

inputName.description: The input tensor the sample binds to. Omit it on a single-input model.

dtype.description: The element type of the sample's binary input.

shape.description: The fully resolved shape of the sample's binary input. A warmup sample has no dynamic axes.

compare.description: What `expected` holds. `tensors`: raw output tensors, compared elementwise under `tolerances`. `normalized`: the family's normalized output, compared field by field, which is what a quantized model uses when its raw tensors are not reproducible.

tolerances.title: Warmup tolerances
tolerances.description: How far a warmup run may drift from its golden before the bundle is refused. Every provider produces slightly different floating-point results, so a tolerance of zero would refuse every GPU.

absolute.description: The largest permitted absolute difference per element.

relative.description: The largest permitted relative difference per element.

boxIou.description: The smallest permitted intersection over union between a golden box and its match, used when `compare` is `normalized` on a detection model.

provenance.title: Provenance
provenance.description: Who published the bundle and what it came from. It is carried into the evidence sidecar, so a result can be traced back to a training run.

publishedAt.description: When the bundle was published, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

sourceModel.description: The upstream model the bundle was exported from.

trainingRun.description: The training run or experiment identifier.

datasetVersion.description: The dataset the model was trained on.

license.description: The license the model is distributed under.

gitRevision.description: The revision of the pipeline that produced the bundle.

topK.description: How many classes the normalized output keeps, after sorting by descending score.

activation.description: The activation applied to the raw logits. `none` means the graph already emits probabilities.

scoreThreshold.description: The lowest score a class needs to appear in the output.

labelsFile.description: The bundle file that maps class indexes to labels.

outputName.description: The output tensor holding the logits. Omit it on a single-output model.

decoder.description: How raw outputs become boxes. `raw`: the graph already emits final boxes and scores. `yolox`: anchor-free grid decoding using `strides`. `ssd`: separate box, score, and class tensors named by `outputNames`. `anchorBoxes`: grid decoding against the `anchors` list.

boxFormat.description: How the decoded box coordinates are laid out before normalization.

boxesNormalized.description: Whether decoded coordinates are already in `[0, 1]`. When `false` they are divided by the model input size and un-letterboxed.

strides.description: The feature-map strides of a grid decoder.

anchors.description: The anchor box sizes as `[width, height]` pairs in model input pixels.

numClasses.description: How many classes the head predicts.

scoreThreshold.description: The lowest score a detection needs to survive filtering.

iouThreshold.description: The intersection over union above which non-maximum suppression drops the weaker box.

classAgnosticNms.description: Whether suppression compares boxes across classes instead of within each class.

labelsFile.description: The bundle file that maps class indexes to labels.

outputNames.title: Output roles
outputNames.description: Which output tensor plays which role, for heads that emit more than one.

numClasses.description: How many classes the head predicts.

activation.description: The activation applied across the class axis. `sigmoid` treats each class independently.

threshold.description: The per-pixel score at which a class claims a pixel, used with `sigmoid` activation.

ignoreIndex.description: A class index excluded from the summary, usually the background.

minRegionPixels.description: The smallest region reported, in source pixels. It suppresses single-pixel speckle.

labelsFile.description: The bundle file that maps class indexes to labels.

outputName.description: The output tensor holding the class map. Omit it on a single-output model.

threshold.description: The score at which the image counts as anomalous. It is republished on every result.

higherIsAnomalous.description: Whether a higher score means more anomalous. Set it to `false` for a similarity score.

scoreOutput.description: The output tensor holding the image-level score.

heatmapOutput.description: The output tensor holding the per-pixel anomaly map. The map is summarized and never published.

maxRegions.description: How many heatmap regions the summary reports.

regionThreshold.description: The per-pixel score at which a heatmap pixel joins a region. It defaults to `threshold`.

executionProvider.title: ONNX Runtime execution provider
executionProvider.description: An execution provider name as ONNX Runtime reports it.

bundlePath.description: A path relative to the bundle root, with `/` separators. It is never absolute and never traverses upward; extraction rejects anything else before this schema is even reached.

hex256.description: A SHA-256 digest as 64 lowercase hex characters, without a prefix.
